page: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is an ARM64-based instance powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) running at 2.3 GHz on the ARMv8 Cortex-A72 microarchitecture. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the single-core performance of the Cortex-A72 processor is modest, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1449.88, placing it in the average tier. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core benchmarks like Geekbench (384.0) and stress-ng multi-core (1449.88) fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth is limited, measuring 10.43 GB/sec for large-block reads and 5.95 GB/sec for large-block writes. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via hardware AES, but advanced vector extensions are absent.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.medium offers a low-cost entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, making it suitable for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core isolation without requiring high memory density or extreme compute power. It is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving with a static throughput of 0.48 GB/sec, simple microservices, development environments, and testing ARM64 compatibility.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.medium is an ARM64-based virtual machine powered by a first-generation AWS Graviton processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes no local storage and no GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks indicate modest single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1449.88, while multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect its single-thread design. The processor supports hardware AES encryption but lacks advanced vector extensions. It delivers a static web serving throughput of 0.48 GB/sec and a prompt processing speed of 21.67 tokens/sec for small language models. Qualitatively, the a1.medium represents a highly cost-efficient entry point for ARM64 development, testing, and lightweight, scale-out applications such as basic web serving or microservices.
